slides.0.title: New York I: the Finger Lakes
slides.0.subtitle: The lake effect, soils and sub-AVAs
slides.1.title: The AVA and its lakes
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Extent
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Approved in 1982; about 5.4 million acres with eleven lakes, in upstate New York about 25 miles south of Lake Ontario, covering 14 counties
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Key lakes
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Most vineyards sit around four lakes: Canandaigua, Keuka, Seneca and Cayuga
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Sub-AVAs
slides.1.content: The Finger Lakes have eleven lakes, but only Cayuga and Seneca are sub-AVAs.
slides.2.title: The lake effect
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Winter
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The lakes add moisture that forms deep snow cover, protecting vines from freezing; Seneca Lake has frozen over only a few times in the past hundred years
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Spring
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Cool lake breezes delay bud-break until frost danger passes
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Autumn
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Warm breezes delay the first frost and lengthen the growing season
slides.2.content: The lake effect = winter protection + a spring delay + an autumn extension.
slides.3.title: Climate figures and soils
slides.3.highlights.0.title: A continental climate
slides.3.highlights.0.content: A growing season of about 190–205 days, 30 to 40 inches of precipitation a year and USDA hardiness zones 5b to 6b
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Soils
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Glacial erosion and deposits created varied soils, generally deep and well drained; Dunkirk clay loam is the most common, and in places such as the west side of Seneca Lake bedrock is close to the surface
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Varieties
slides.3.highlights.2.content: More than 60 varieties are grown, with Riesling the most emblematic; about 832 acres in 2024
slides.3.content: The Finger Lakes combine a continental climate with lake buffering, so winter risk is reduced but not removed.
Which are the two sub-AVAs of the Finger Lakes?
A. Cayuga Lake and Seneca Lake
In which year was the Seneca Lake AVA approved?
What is the lakes' main spring effect on vineyards?
A. Delaying bud-break to avoid frost
